idea_summary:
WhyC — YC 풍자 카운터프로덕트.

문제: YC 배치를 받은 스타트업들이 Demo Day 이후 6개월이 지나도 workatastartup.com에 "엔지니어/인턴 구함" 공고만 올리고 정작 제품을 출시하지 못하는 패턴. (예시: workatastartup.com/jobs/82957)

해결: YC 회사의 잡 포스팅 URL(또는 회사 설명)을 입력받아 멀티에이전트 파이프라인이 1일 이내에 호스팅된 *작동하는* 프리뷰를 자동 생성한다. "그들이 6개월 걸리는 걸 우리는 1일에 만든다"가 헤드라인 도발.

핵심 차별점 — 단순 코드젠이 아니라 self-improvement loop:
1) URL → Spec 추출 (Gemini)
2) Spec → 디자인 토큰 + Next.js 코드 + 핵심 API 1~2개
3) Cloud Run 배포
4) Phoenix MCP가 trace 조회 → LLM-as-judge가 "프리뷰가 추출 spec과 일치하는가" 평가 → 미흡한 flow만 재생성 → 수렴까지 반복

스택 (해카톤 강제 — 변경 불가):
- Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform / ADK (code-owned runtime)
- Google Cloud Agent Builder (오케스트레이션)
- Arize Phoenix MCP + OpenInference 자동 계측 (Arize 트랙)
- Cloud Run 배포, Secret Manager
- 웹 플랫폼 (Next.js 권장)

타겟 사용자:
- Primary: 인디 해커 / 시리얼 파운더 ("왜 저들이 못 만들지?" 진영)
- Secondary: VC·엔젤 (포트폴리오 회사의 *실제 빌드 능력* 진단 도구)
- Demo 시청자: 해카톤 심사위원

브랜드 톤:
- 어그로·도발 카피 풀세게 (제품 헤드라인, Devpost text, README, 웹사이트)
- "WHILE YC HIRES, WE SHIP" 류
- 픽셀 퍼펙트 sleek UI (브루털리즘 아님, 진지하게 끝난 작품처럼)
- YC 오렌지에 대한 시각적 패러디 OK, 공식 로고/워드마크 직접 사용은 금지

데모 영상(3분) 톤:
- 자랑·와우 중심, 특정 YC 회사명·로고는 화면에 안 띄움
- 합성 JD 또는 익명화한 케이스로 1개 end-to-end 시연
- "input → 24h 후 deployed URL" 비포·애프터 구도

성공 기준 (해카톤 채점):
- Stage 1 pass: Gemini + Arize MCP + Cloud Run + 공개 레포 + OSI 라이선스 + 3분 영상
- Stage 2 4축:
  · Tech Implementation: ADK + Phoenix 깊은 통합, self-improvement loop가 코드로 증명
  · Design: WhyC 자체 UI + 생성된 프리뷰 둘 다 finished 작품
  · Potential Impact: "founder가 1일에 valid prototype 보유" 함의
  · Idea Quality: YC 풍자 × 자기개선 에이전트 결합은 갤러리에서 unique
- Arize 트랙 보너스: self-improvement loop 명시적 시연

팀: 2인 (대표자 Sejun Kim, centisgood@gmail.com).
마감: 2026-06-11 14:00 PT (오늘 기준 +36일).
트랙: Arize.

제약 (실격 방지):
- 5월 5일 이후 신규 창작. pf 플러그인 코드 재사용 금지(메서돌로지 영감만).
- 영상에서 특정 YC 회사명·로고 금지 (카테고리적 풍자만).
- AWS·OpenAI·Anthropic API를 에이전트 백본으로 사용 금지.

target_persona.profile: Indie hacker / serial founder who watches YC Demo Day cohorts and asks 'why can't they ship?' — wants to weaponize that frustration into a working preview to mock and to actually use
target_persona.primary_pain: Sees YC-backed startups posting 'hiring engineers/interns' 6+ months after Demo Day with no shipped product, while their own ideas similarly stall before reaching a working hosted prototype

jobs_to_be_done.functional: Turn a YC job-posting URL (or company description) into a hosted, working Next.js preview on Cloud Run within 24 hours, with a self-improvement loop (Phoenix MCP + LLM-as-judge) that regenerates weak flows until the deployed preview matches the extracted spec
jobs_to_be_done.emotional: Feel vindicated and a little smug — 'while they hire, we ship' — confident that the satire is backed by a real, finished artifact judges and peers can click
jobs_to_be_done.social: Be perceived as the team that out-shipped a YC batch in a weekend — credible in indie-hacker / Arize-track / Google Cloud agent-builder circles as serious agent engineers, not just shitposters

must_have_constraints.value: Hackathon-locked stack: Gemini ADK + Google Cloud Agent Builder + Arize Phoenix MCP + Cloud Run + Next.js. AWS / OpenAI / Anthropic APIs forbidden as agent backbone.
OSI-approved open-source license required for hackathon Stage-1 pass; public repo mandatory.
Originality rule: all creative work dated on or after 2026-05-05; no reuse of preview-forge plugin code (methodology inspiration only).
Trademark hygiene: no YC company names or official logos in the 3-minute demo video; categorical satire only. YC-orange visual parody acceptable, official wordmark use forbidden.
End-to-end pipeline must produce a deployed Cloud Run URL within 24 hours of URL submission (the headline claim).

killer_feature:
Self-improvement loop: Phoenix MCP queries the agent's own OpenInference traces, an LLM-as-judge scores whether the deployed preview matches the extracted spec, and only the under-spec flows are regenerated until convergence — distinguishing WhyC from one-shot codegen demos.

UX cadence: Hybrid. The user sees real-time agent progress for ~10 minutes until the first Cloud Run URL is live (visible spec-fit score, e.g. 71%). The self-improvement loop then runs for hours in the background, raising spec-fit with each iteration (84% → 92% → 96% converged). The 'we ship in a day' headline covers the fully-converged window.
non_goals: Not a YC accelerator competitor — no funding, mentorship, or batch programming
Not a general code-review or refactoring tool — input is a URL/description, not an existing repo
Not a no-code site builder for end-users — the user-facing artifact is a generated preview, not a builder UI
Not a production-grade hosting platform — Cloud Run previews are demo artifacts, not SLA-backed products
Not naming or shaming specific YC companies — satire stays categorical; no real names/logos in the video
Not a replacement for human product design — generated preview anchors discussion, doesn't end it
success_metric: Hackathon Stage-2 four-axis scoring: (1) Tech Implementation — ADK + Phoenix deep integration with self-improvement loop proven in code; (2) Design — both WhyC's own UI and the generated previews read as finished work; (3) Potential Impact — 'founder holds a valid prototype in 1 day' narrative lands; (4) Idea Quality — YC-satire × self-improving-agent combo is unique in the gallery. Bonus: explicit Arize-track self-improvement loop demo in the 3-minute video.
